newsitem.title: USA: AmEx net fueled by Financial Advisors unit.
newsitem.headline: AmEx net fueled by Financial Advisors unit.

text.p: American Express Co's record first quarter 1997 net income of $454 million was fueled by a 21 percent increase in net income at American Express Financial Advisors.
The $454 million net income was 14.6 percent higher than the $396 million in the first quarter of 1996.

The net income in the financial advisors unit rose to $157 million from $130 million a year ago, while net income in travel related services was $315 million, an increase of 10 percent from the $286 million a year ago.
Earnings-per-share in the first quarter rose to $0.94 from $0.80 a year ago.

American Express said revenue and earnings growth in the Financial Advisors unit benefited from higher fee revenues due to an increase in managed assets and growth in distribution fees primarily from record sales of mutual funds.

In Travel Related Services, net revenues rose to $2.97 billion from $2.78 billion a year ago, an increase of 6.9 percent. Excluding the impact of securitizing a portion of the card portfolio and a reduction in investments related to the consolidation of certain legal entitties, revenues rose nine percent.

American Express said an improvement in billed business in Travel Related Services reflects the 8.3 per rise in cards outstanding to 41.9 million worldwide and higher spending per cardmember. The company said spending grew in part due to the benefits of rewards programs and expanded merchant coverage. Average basic cardmember spending rose 5.0 percent to $1,498.

The charge card provision for losses declined 9.4 percent to $190 million. The charge card provision for losses declined particularly in Latin America and the small business card portfolio. The lending provision for losses rose 12.3 percent to $211 million primarily because of growth in outstanding loans.
Total card billed business worldwide was $47.9 billion, an increase of 15.3 percent. Within the U.S., card billed business rose 16.5 percent to $34.6 billion.
The American Express Bank had first quarter net income of $20 million, up from $19 million a year ago.

The growth in earnings mainly reflected higher revenues due to increased net interest income on loans and investments. American Express said this was largely offset by higher operating expenses due primarily to systems technology investment.

American Express said that during the quarter the bank unit had an $18 million loan recovery from Peru, which was used to increase the reserve for credit losses. The bank also received an unfavorable court ruling relating to the collapse of the Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) in 1991. The court in effect denied American Express Bank's claims to $24 million in funds that it claimed as setoffs against BCCI obligations then oustanding to the bank. American Express said the matter is not expected to have a material impact on the bank's results.
